reasons: Directionally correct for us as Customer: the edit tightens an audit obligation binding Corio (our party) by fixing 30 days' prior written notice, confining inspections to normal business hours, requiring the auditor to be bound by confidentiality, and barring access to our systems/networks/facilities — exactly the AUDIT preferred position.

Rule coverage is complete: frequency (once per calendar year) and cost allocation (Commerce One bears cost unless >5% underpayment) already comply and are correctly left untouched, and the independent CPA acceptable to us is preserved, so all four rule parameters (frequency, notice, cost, system access) are satisfied.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic is not disqualifying here: only one sentence was replaced and two limiting clauses inserted; the surrounding record-retention, shortfall/overpayment and cost-shifting language is verbatim, so the high changed-character ratio reflects the short target sentence rather than an over-broad rewrite.
Comment is accurate, on-tone, prefixed, explains what changed and why, and offers the 15-day fallback consistent with the playbook.

Minor caution (not a basis for failure): the cross-reference to 'Section 10' for confidentiality obligations is not verifiable from the supplied paragraphs — confirm the correct confidentiality section number or use a generic reference to the Agreement's confidentiality provisions before sending.
